name: Cheese pashtida — with spinach, optimized (פשטידת גבינות ותרד)

source.author: Optimized version of cheese_pashtida_base
source.notes: Dual-lens-optimized version of cheese_pashtida_base, adopted per user request (user chose spinach as the add-in the base recipe offered as optional). Changes from the base: 150 g fresh spinach folded in raw (wilts in the bake — the single biggest fix, since the base recipe has almost no folate/fiber without a vegetable), feta trimmed from 250 g to 180 g to cut sodium, flour swapped to whole spelt, no added salt anywhere. Everything else identical (4 eggs, cottage, white cheese, yellow cheese, cream cheese, baking powder). Analyzed for the whole bake; per_serving = batch ÷ 8 (~190 g). Raw-spinach folate is used for the batch total; actual folate retention after baking is somewhat lower (egg custards shield it better than boiling, but some loss is normal) — still a large net gain over the base recipe's near-zero folate. Estimate.

serving_desc: ≈190 g slice (batch ÷8) — side or light main; 2 slices = a fuller meal

ingredients.note: whole-grain swap for fiber vs the base recipe's white flour
trimmed from the base recipe's 250 g — cuts sodium, keeps the tang
folded in raw — the big nutritional fix vs the base recipe
feta + yellow cheese already salt the dish

steps: Whisk the eggs; mix in the cottage, white cheese, whole-spelt flour and baking powder.
Fold in the yellow cheese, feta, cream cheese and the raw chopped spinach.
Pour into a greased/lined baking dish and level the top.
Bake at 180 °C, top-bottom heat, ~35-45 min until set (not wobbly) and golden on top; a knife in the middle should come out clean.

batch_totals.note: Whole bake (8 slices), optimized. Vs the base recipe (per slice ~131 kcal / 12.8 g protein / ~0.1 g fiber / ~430 mg sodium / near-zero folate): nearly identical protein, meaningfully more fiber (spinach), real folate (spinach's biggest contribution), and lower sodium (trimmed feta + no added salt).

him.verdict: This is the version of the cheese pashtida worth making: still ~12.5 g protein for only 127 kcal (~9.9 g protein per 100 kcal — essentially unchanged from the base, still near the top of your library), but now with real fiber and folate from 150 g of spinach, and lower sodium from trimming the feta and skipping added salt. The egg-and-four-cheese base was already an excellent protein source; folding in the vegetable the original poster suggested fixes its one real gap without costing you anything on protein or calories.
flags: ~12.5 g protein / 127 kcal slice (~9.9 g protein per 100 kcal)
~0.7 g fiber/slice — spinach turns this from near-zero to a real contribution
lower sodium (~355 mg/slice) — trimmed feta + no added salt
still very high calcium + choline from eggs/cheeses
near-identical protein and calories to the base recipe
suggested_mods: Great as-is; pair with a lean protein for a fuller cut meal
Push spinach to 200 g if you want even more fiber/folate — macros barely move
Serve with tomato for a vitamin-C boost alongside the iron

her_preconception.verdict: A big step up from the base recipe for her: 150 g of spinach is a genuine folate contributor (her #1 preconception nutrient), on top of the choline (4 eggs), calcium and protein the cheese base already brought — and sodium is now meaningfully lower. Fully baked custard, so the spinach and eggs are cooked through. One flag carries over: feta is a brined cheese, baked through here (cooked = considered safe), but verify it's pasteurized. This is now a dish worth making for her regularly, not just an occasional protein source.
prenatal_highlights: real folate from 150 g spinach — her top preconception nutrient, missing in the base recipe
lower sodium than the base; fully baked

safety_advisories.note: Feta is a brined cheese — Listeria risk unless pasteurized. It's baked through here (cooked = considered safe); verify it's a pasteurized feta.
safety_advisories.swap: verify pasteurized, or use more cottage/white cheese in its place

suggested_mods: No changes needed — this is now a solid folate + protein + calcium dish for her
Serve with tomato/pepper for extra vitamin C to aid iron absorption

adopted_note: Adopted 2026-10-23 as the spinach-optimized version of the cheese pashtida (supersedes cheese_pashtida_base for actual use — user chose spinach as the add-in). Per slice (of 8, ~190 g): ~127 kcal, 12.5 g protein, 0.7 g fiber, ~44 mcg DFE folate, ~355 mg sodium. him 9 / her 8. Standing spec: 150 g fresh spinach folded in raw, feta trimmed to 180 g, whole-spelt flour, no added salt. Bake 180 C top-bottom ~35-45 min. Verify feta pasteurized.
cooking_guide: Whisk the eggs well, then stir in the cottage cheese, white cheese, whole-spelt flour and baking powder until smooth.
Fold in the chopped yellow cheese, crumbled feta, cream cheese, and the raw chopped spinach — no need to pre-cook it, it wilts fully in the bake.
Taste the raw batter before considering any salt — the feta and yellow cheese almost certainly cover it; this version adds none.
Pour into a greased or lined baking dish and level the top.

Bake at 180 °C with top-bottom heat ~35-45 min until the center is set (not wobbly) and the top is golden; a knife in the middle should come out clean. Check your specific pan size — a wider/shallower dish bakes faster.
Rest 10 min before slicing so it holds together.
Tip: a little lemon zest or fresh dill folded in with the spinach brightens the whole dish.
